Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one

Strand: Family Suggested vocabulary: father, mother, sister, brother, baby, aunt, uncle,
Topic 3.1: Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary, part of Family Suggested vocabulary: father, mother, sister, brother, baby, aunt, uncle, in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can we become better listeners?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: A learner develops active listening skills as they listen to sound from oral texts and pronounce them correctly.

• Self-efficacy: learner’s knowledge of their family is enhanced as they use dialogues/rhymes/tongue twisters/ language games/ songs about family.

Values:
• Respect is promoted as the learner shows positive regard for self and others as they role play during the lesson.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
• Life skills (gender issues) – The learner’s sense of self awareness is increased as he or she sings rhymes, says tongue twisters and recites poems

related to the theme.

Link to other Learning Areas:

• Listening attentively is emphasised in Kiswahili and Indigenous Languages Activities.

d) advocate the need for accurate

• Learners are guided to listen to an

audio visual clip and point out the

sounds of the letters: q, r, s, t, u, v, w,

x, y, z as modelled by the teacher.

• Learners are guided to individually say

the sounds /q/, /r/, /s/, t, //ʌ /, /v/, /w/,

/x/, /y/ and /z /.

• Learners with low vision are guided

to view a chart featuring the letters

and say the corresponding sounds

while learners with blindness to say

any target letter and the partner to say

the corresponding sound.

• Learners to role play responding to

simple instructions using the new

words related to the theme.

• In pairs, guide learners to use

dialogues/rhymes/tongue twisters/

language games/ songs to practise

vocabulary related to the theme.
